chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about the teeth, so he said: 'These, with regards to the wergild, are the same'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on blood money for damaged teeth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that in Shia jurisprudence, all teeth are considered equal in value for blood money (diyah), a ruling that simplifies compensation calculations by treating any single tooth injury uniformly. This consensus among the Imams reflects a practical approach to bodily injury law, ensuring equitable treatment regardless of which specific tooth is damaged. It underscores the principle of uniformity in physical compensation within the broader framework of Islamic penal law.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Usma Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,
